candidate_diagrams.claim: Dualizing a crystal negates weights, reverses colored arrows, swaps epsilon/phi, and sends (b1⊗b2)^vee to b2^vee⊗b1^vee; in the examples the sl2 chain is self-dual, the sl3 chain reverses into B(lambda2), and the tensor square splits as B(2) disjoint union B(0).
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The core claims are concrete finite colored graphs plus an explicit vertex map and tensor-factor reversal, so one small diagram can make the arrow reversal and tensor swap immediately checkable.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Show B(1): v0 -1-> v1 and its dual v1^vee -1-> v0^vee with map v1^vee↦v0, v0^vee↦v1 and negated weights; show the sl3 chain u1 -1-> u2 -2-> u3 reversing to u3^vee -2-> u2^vee -1-> u1^vee and map to B(lambda2); optionally show tensor dual map (b1⊗b2)^vee↦b2^vee⊗b1^vee with B(2) chain plus isolated B(0). Keep as a finite worked example, not a general decomposition diagram.

candidate_diagrams.claim: Under the stated hypotheses and choice input, an isomorphism Phi identifies M and its crystal basis with an algebraic direct sum of simple highest-weight modules and a disjoint union of canonical highest-weight crystals; each connected component has one highest-weight vertex and is generated by lowering operators.
candidate_diagrams.kind: crystal component decomposition and equivariant map
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The theorem’s central content is the correspondence between module decomposition, crystal connected components, and the map Phi. A schematic disjoint-union diagram would clarify the component bijection and lowering-generated subcrystals.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Draw M with crystal basis B, the module isomorphism Phi:M→⊕_{j∈J}V(lambda_j), and induced crystal bijection B→⊔_{j∈J}B(lambda_j); depict two sample components with highest vertices b_j and arrows labeled by lowering colors, and annotate each component as F(b_j). Explicitly allow J infinite and indicate local weight finiteness rather than implying a finite total decomposition.

candidate_diagrams.claim: For each residue color, the Fock-space node action decomposes into finite Boolean cubes of two-vertex strings; E_i removes and F_i adds a residue-i node, while the proof checks mixed commutators locally on overlapping finite wedges before applying the rank-one Serre implication.
candidate_diagrams.kind: colored Boolean cube / local operator action
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The proof relies on finite cube structure and local add/remove moves as its explicit mechanism for integrability and same-color commutators; a small partition-node example would show what the cube vertices and operators mean.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Show a finite fixed-residue-i orbit as a Boolean cube whose vertices are partitions obtained by choosing subsets of a finite family of addable/removable residue-i nodes; label each edge by F_i in the add direction and E_i in reverse, with one representative partition and residue marks. If adding a second color, mark only the overlapping finite-square calculation used for [E_i,F_j]=0, avoiding any suggestion that the full affine relations follow from one cube alone.
